decision: Measured the machine and the clone before designing: 2 vCPU, 3 GB RAM, no SCons, 1.2 GB of git history.
why: A full engine build would take hours and could run out of memory, so verification had to use the official binary.
result: No source build this session.

decision: Merge upstream tags into main behind a thin allowlist. Do not rebase and do not rebrand every file.
why: Merging keeps public history stable and limits 4.8 conflicts to the few files gai edits.
result: Accepted; enforced by bin/gai upstream check.

decision: Kept the Godot project in game/ instead of the repository root.
why: The root holds 14k engine files; a project.godot there would make Godot import the engine source.
result: The editor opens game/ directly.

decision: Chose one Python CLI over an MCP server or an editor panel.
why: Agents already have a shell, and the CLI works in pi, opencode, CI, and a terminal with no extra process.
result: Accepted.

decision: Changed version.py name to gai and the website URL. Kept short_name=godot and the godot binary name.
why: methods.py:268 asserts short_name is godot, and platform/linuxbsd/SCsub:44 hardcodes #bin/godot. Changing them adds build conflicts for no visible gain.
result: The window title and version header read gai.

decision: Check runs three stages: import assets, parse every .gd with --check-only, then run the main scene.
why: Godot 4.7.2 exits 0 on parse and runtime errors, so an exit-code check passes a broken game.
result: Parse error and runtime error both fail check; the clean project passes.

decision: Installed the official engine through bin/gai engine install.
why: This proves the download, SHA-512 check, and extraction with the real release.
result: 139.6 MiB downloaded; version 4.7.2.stable.official.ed1daf0bf; exit 0.

decision: Tested the upstream tools against a synthetic 4.8 tag with a clean merge, a README conflict, an abort, and an out-of-layer edit.
why: The real 4.8 tag does not exist, so the merge runbook needed a local proof.
result: 5 tests pass.

decision: Push main to git@github.com:jerryshell/gai.git.
why: The target repository was empty and the user asked for it to be the distribution.
result: open

decision: Pushed main to origin at 4ca7679ba3.
why: The empty target repository now holds the full Godot history and the gai layer.
result: ok

decision: Stripped a leading -- from bin/gai run arguments before calling the engine.
why: The documented run -- --headless command reached the engine as --, so the engine ignored --headless and tried to open a display.
result: `run -- --headless --quit-after 2` exits 0 and prints the scene ready line.

decision: Taught the merge command to resolve version.py by taking upstream file and re-applying name and website.
why: A real 4.8 bump conflicts on the adjacent website and docs lines; the brand is two declarative keys, so the resolution is deterministic.
result: 7 tests pass, including a version bump and a version bump plus README conflict.

decision: Independent review found a stale-engine gate hole, a missed SHADER ERROR, a false input rule, and a thin layer guard.
why: The findings were specific and reproduced, so I fixed them before calling 0.1.0 done.
result: 5 fixed; repo visibility is the owner's action.

decision: Made check refuse an engine or version.py that does not match the recorded upstream tag, including two-part tags such as 4.8-stable.
why: The old doctor check silently skipped 4.8-stable, so a forgotten engine install would leave every gate green on the old engine.
result: Stale engine and stale version.py both fail check.

decision: Added SHADER ERROR to the error scan and an end-to-end test that injects a parse error.
why: The scan missed one of Godot's error kinds, and no test proved check can fail.
result: Parse error exits 1; clean project exits 0.

decision: Corrected the input action rule in AGENTS.md and the skill.
why: Godot prints an error for an undeclared action, and check catches it; the old text told agents the gate was blind.
result: Verified with a headless run.

decision: Added a required file list and a clean-tree check before an upstream merge.
why: A deleted core file or a dirty tree could leave the layer check green.
result: 9 tests pass.

decision: Added the version-string update step to the upstream runbook.
why: A 4.8 merge leaves 4.7 strings in the docs and the editor rewrites project.godot.
result: The runbook now greps for the old version.

decision: Extended the layer check to untracked files outside owned paths.
why: A committed diff cannot see a local engine file, and the review showed the check stayed green with one present.
result: 10 tests pass.

decision: Replaced the thin-layer allowlist with feature-owned divergence. The engine is now a first-class part of gai.
why: The product is AI-native and needs deep engine changes; the thin layer blocked the product.
result: 11 upstream tests pass; check and doctor pass.

decision: Recorded .NET web export as a planned high-risk feature. Upstream 4.7.2 refuses it; the available patch targets 4.8-dev and Windows.
why: The requested feature is allowed by the new architecture but still needs a custom engine build and a base-version decision.
result: Not active; blocked on a build platform.

decision: Chose the engine agent bridge as the first vertical AI-native feature.
why: The CLI cannot see live editor state; an in-engine bridge gives agents scene, input, and screenshot control.
result: Planned; design recorded.
